system.name: Shopwell
system.purpose: A small online store: customers browse a product catalog, place orders, pay invoices, and receive shipments. Five bounded contexts — Catalog, Orders, Inventory, Billing, Shipping — coordinated through a shared Identity kernel.
system.narrative:
A customer browses and adds a to their . Checkout calls , which reserves stock through the seam — an anticorruption layer that translates between Orders' `LineItem` vocabulary and Inventory's `StockItem` vocabulary. Once the reservation lands, Orders publishes ; consumes the event to open an , and picks up the same event to schedule a shipment.
Two cross-cutting values live in the shared kernel rather than being re-declared in each context. A duplicated `Money` struct would inevitably drift — on currency-code casing, on rounding, on whether negative amounts are allowed. The kernel makes the sharing explicit and load-bearing.

shared-kernel.name: Identity kernel
shared-kernel.description: Cross-context values: how customers are named, how money is denominated. Every context references these directly; no context redeclares them.
shared-kernel.rationale: `Money` re-declared per context would diverge on rounding, on currency-code casing, on negative-amount handling. Lifting it (and `CustomerId`) to a kernel makes one definition load-bearing for every context that uses it, and gives a single home for the arithmetic invariant below.

term.name: `CustomerId`
term.definition: A stable opaque string identifying one customer across every context. Issued by the (out-of-process) identity service at signup; never reused, never reassigned.

term.name: `Money`
term.definition: An amount paired with a currency code: `{amount: bigint, currency: "USD" | "EUR" | "GBP"}`. Amounts are integer minor units (cents) to avoid float drift. Negative amounts represent refunds.
term.equality: Two Money values are equal iff their `amount` and `currency` match. Arithmetic across mismatched currencies is forbidden — see .

invariant.name: Money operations preserve currency
invariant.statement: Adding, subtracting, or comparing Money values requires both operands to share a currency. No implicit conversion. Mixing currencies is a programming error, not a runtime fallback.
invariant.rationale: Implicit FX conversion at arithmetic sites hides the rate, the rounding rule, and the moment in time the rate applied. Forcing explicit conversion at boundaries (where the rate is named) keeps Money predictable end-to-end.

overlay.name: Tax jurisdiction overlay
overlay.description: Per-deployment tax behavior. The same Shopwell binary serves multiple regions; the overlay is the seam where regional tax law enters the system without polluting 's core model.

items.item: EU deployments compute VAT at invoice time, with reverse-charge for B2B.
US deployments compute sales tax per shipping address; no central rate table is canonical.
UK deployments behave like EU for VAT but use a separate registration-number namespace.

invariant.statement: The overlay supplies tax rates; never hardcodes a percentage.
invariant.rationale: Hardcoded rates leak the deployment's tax regime into a context that should be installation-agnostic. The overlay is the only place rates live.

deliberate-omission.reason: Shopwell does not model recommendation engines or cross-customer behavioral analytics. They would require a sixth context with its own consent model and data-retention rules — out of scope for the demo, and a substantial product decision rather than a technical one.
deliberate-omission.trigger: The product team commits to a recommendations roadmap.
A regulatory requirement (e.g. GDPR cohort-tracking rules) forces explicit modeling.

deliberate-omission.reason: A customer might want to hold balances in multiple currencies and pay invoices from a chosen wallet. Today every settles in the invoice's currency only; FX happens at the payment gateway, not inside Shopwell. The wallet feature would require a ledger model that doesn't have.
deliberate-omission.trigger: A high-volume B2B customer asks to settle EU and UK invoices from a single GBP wallet.
